signals.signal: H1-2026 Interim Report (published 06/08/2026): NLB d.d. (Slovenia) operated 371 branches at 30/06/2026, down from 386 at 30/06/2025 and 381 at 31/12/2025. In H1 2026 the bank opened three new branches built on its 'cash-light concept' promoting digital/self-service and reducing cash handling; one newly established branch was fitted with a Cash Deposit System (CDS) letting legal entities deposit daily business cash. Group net fee income from Credit cards and ATMs reached EUR 71.965m in H1 2026 (from EUR 67.657m H1 2025, +6%).
signals.source_name: NLB Group Interim Report January-June 2026 (pp. header metrics, Retail chapter)
signals.implies: Branch network is shrinking while each remaining branch is being re-tooled around self-service; the 'cash-light' + CDS rollout is a live cash-automation/recycler and self-service deposit programme. Printec cash-automation/recyclers and self-service/ATM lines map directly; managed services fit the migration of manned desks to devices.
signals.likelihood: Programme already in execution; further CDS/self-service device rollout across 371-branch network over 6-12 months is highly likely
signals.followup: Identify CDS/recycler vendor NLB is standardising on; quantify how many of 371 branches still have manned cash desks vs self-service deposit.

signals.signal: H1-2026 report: NLB streamlined merchant onboarding so existing clients can order any POS terminal type - traditional, mobile or web - fully online, paperless, via Rekono digital identification; launched a Merchant Portal business-analytics module; completed a 'major POS terminal implementation project for a large merchant' enabling multiple business activities on a single POS terminal with automatic settlement; and expanded acquiring for micro-merchants via partnerships with fiscal cash-register providers.
signals.source_name: NLB Group Interim Report January-June 2026 (Retail & CIB card-acquiring chapters)
signals.implies: NLB is actively modernising acquiring infrastructure and merchant POS estate with digital onboarding. Printec POS/acquiring and digital-onboarding/eKYC lines are directly relevant; the single-terminal multi-activity project signals appetite for smart-POS/software-POS and terminal-management (TMS) capability.
signals.likelihood: Acquiring modernisation is an ongoing multi-year theme; further POS/soft-POS and eKYC procurement likely within 12 months
signals.followup: Determine POS hardware/TMS supplier(s) for the large-merchant single-terminal project; whether Bankart processes these transactions (it does for most SI banks).

signals.signal: H1-2026 investor presentation restates Strategy 2030: 'Accelerate cash transition across SEE' as a payments pillar; digital penetration 65% at H1 2026 targeting >80% by 2030; complete technology transformation to microservices by 2030; consumer-finance STP >80% in Slovenia (95% group target). Financial ambition: >EUR 50bn assets, >EUR 2bn recurring revenues, >EUR 1bn profit; CIR to low-40s%; normalised RoE >15%.
signals.source_name: NLB Group Presentation 1H 2026 (Outlook & Strategy / Digital slides)
signals.implies: 'Accelerate cash transition' + full tech transformation + higher STP frame a group-wide, multi-country demand for self-service cash automation (recyclers to displace teller cash), digital onboarding/eKYC and managed services. Printec's 17-country footprint aligns with NLB's SEE roll-out logic; group-standardised device/platform deals are the prize.
signals.likelihood: Strategy is board-committed to 2030; procurement waves across NLB SEE subsidiaries over the coming years are likely
signals.followup: Map which NLB SEE subsidiaries (Serbia, N. Macedonia, BiH, Montenegro, Kosovo) are running self-service/recycler tenders; watch for a group Capital Markets Day update.

signals.entity: OTP banka d.d. / OTP Skupina Slovenija
signals.signal: Unaudited H1-2026 results (published 05/08/2026): OTP Group Slovenia net profit EUR 128m; ROE 13.9% group / 14.0% bank; total assets EUR 15.7bn; gross loans +6.7% to EUR 8.3bn; deposits EUR 12.6bn; LTD 65%; total capital ratio 20.1%; LCR 349%; NIM 3.04%. The integration of OTP Skladi (asset management) completed as a milestone; the bank is rolling out a new 'Value Streams' operating model to become faster and more agile; re-awarded Euromoney 'Best Bank in Slovenia'.
signals.source_name: OTP banka - 'OTP Skupina Slovenija v prvem polletju 2026' press release
signals.implies: OTP Slovenia (formed from SKB + Nova KBM merger) is the country's second-largest bank consolidating asset-management and re-platforming its operating model - a window for self-service, cash-automation and channel rationalisation across a merged, still partly duplicated branch/ATM estate. Printec ATM/self-service, cash automation, POS and managed services all map.
signals.likelihood: Post-merger fleet consolidation and standardisation is an active multi-year programme; device/managed-service tenders plausible in 6-12 months
signals.followup: Obtain OTP SI current ATM/branch counts and merger fleet-harmonisation plan (SKB NCR vs Nova KBM legacy estate); identify incumbent ATM vendor/maintenance provider.

signals.signal: Public security notice (06/08/2026): OTP banka reports a recent cluster of card-fraud cases via ATM skimming - devices copying magnetic-stripe data plus hidden cameras/overlay keypads to capture PINs - and warns customers to inspect card slots/keypads before use.
signals.source_name: OTP banka security notice - ATM skimming abuse
signals.implies: A live skimming wave on OTP's ATM fleet creates near-term demand for anti-skimming hardware, EMV/mag-stripe hardening, ATM security modules and transaction-monitoring/fraud analytics. Printec HSM/security, transaction monitoring and ATM/self-service (with anti-skimming) lines map; also relevant to AML/compliance.
signals.likelihood: Reactive security spend on affected ATM estate is likely in the short term
signals.followup: Check whether OTP SI is procuring anti-skimming / fraud-monitoring upgrades; whether Bankart (its processor) handles fraud detection centrally.

signals.signal: Bankart, described on its own site as 'the leading Slovenian company in the field of processing of modern payment instruments', provides ATM and POS acquiring processing, management and control of ATM and POS networks (terminal management), card-issuing processing/CMS, instant-payment/SEPA clearing and settlement, card-lifecycle management, Apple/Google Pay, e-commerce and fraud prevention/security - and markets instant-payment infrastructure to central banks, citing deployments already operating in the Eurozone. Development is organised into 17 agile teams across five business areas and four technical platforms.
signals.source_name: Bankart - Acquiring / Payment Systems and Services / Home (EN)
signals.implies: Bankart is the incumbent national processor driving ATM/POS estates and TMS for most Slovenian banks - a structural barrier to Printec's POS/acquiring, TMS and transaction-monitoring in Slovenia, since processing/driving is centralised here rather than bank-by-bank. But Bankart is also a potential channel/partner for hardware and self-service devices, and its central-bank instant-payments export ambition signals appetite for infrastructure partners.
signals.likelihood: Structural incumbency is stable; partnership/hardware-supply angle is the realistic 6-12 month path
signals.followup: Clarify Bankart's ownership (bank consortium) and which SI banks self-drive vs use Bankart; explore Bankart as reseller/partner for recyclers and anti-skimming rather than competing head-on.

signals.entity: Intesa Sanpaolo Bank (Slovenia) / Intesa Sanpaolo Group
signals.signal: No Slovenia-specific H1-2026 disclosure located this run; the only H1-2026 material available is the Intesa Sanpaolo Group (Italy) 1H26 results (29/07/2026), which are group-level (2026 net-income guidance upgraded to >EUR 10bn, >20% RoE) and carry no Slovenia subsidiary fleet/branch/ATM detail. Intesa SI is a smaller universal player in the market.
signals.implies: Intesa SI remains an unquantified prospect: no primary Slovenia-level fleet figure obtained. Any Printec opportunity there needs subsidiary-level disclosure not yet found.
signals.followup: Pull Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenija local annual report / AJPES filing for branch, ATM and card figures; check local press for any digitalisation announcements.

coverage_notes: Fresh run (no checkpoint existed). WebSearch budget was fully exhausted (200/200) at the very start of this run, so all discovery was done by direct primary-source fetching (curl with desktop UA + local pdfminer.six extraction) against banks' own IR/press. Covered: NLB Group H1-2026 interim report + presentation (branches, cash-light/CDS, POS onboarding, card fees, Strategy 2030); OTP Skupina Slovenija H1-2026 press release (EUR 15.7bn, ROE 13.9%, OTP Skladi integration, Value Streams model) + OTP ATM-skimming security notice; Bankart service pages (national ATM/POS/TMS processor, instant payments, fraud prevention). Group-level financials verified from PDFs; every figure cited to a primary URL and dated.
access_issues: WebSearch unavailable (session budget 200/200 consumed before this bank was reached) - all sourcing done via curl/pdfminer. NLB branch/ATM locator is an AEM SPA: the branchsearch.search.json endpoint returned 403 to anonymous POST and requires a live browser session + CSRF/cookie state (a CSRF-token POST only triggered an AEM content-modify response, not data), so a machine-readable per-site ATM/deposit-capable count could not be pulled this run - escalation to Claude-in-Chrome would be needed. Bankart /en/news/ returns a WordPress HTTP 500; /en/about-us/ and /en/services/ 404/500 on some paths (used working home + acquiring + payment-systems pages instead). Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenija has no located Slovenia-specific H1-2026 disclosure.
